topIssues.title: contracts-bedrock: dispute game gas and bond sizing under Glamsterdam
topIssues.author: conr2d
topIssues.body:
On Sepolia under Glamsterdam, the receipts of the four dispute game creations I traced show 4.4–4.6 times the gas of a local Osaka replay of the same transactions. The replay (`cast run --quick`) starts from the parent block's state, so the ratio may include a pre-state difference as well as the fork rules. It also does not separate [EIP-8037](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8037) from the other repricings these transactions exercise. EIP-8037 state gas dominates, though: new accounts, code and storage slots make up 86–88% of each receipt's gas.

| Game type | Glamsterdam gas | Osaka gas (replay) |
|---|---:|---:|
| 9 `SuperFaultDisputeGame` | 2,455,999 | 532,891 |
| 1 `PermissionedDisputeGame` | 2,103,594 | 456,482 |
| 42 (Celo) | 1,749,492 | 401,050 |
| 5 `SuperPermissionedDisputeGame` | 1,066,545 | 235,295 |

**Bonds.** The 12 depth-1 `move`s I traced on type 9 games cost 976,066–976,078 gas, against 254,106–254,118 in Osaka replays. The [bond incentives spec](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/blob/main/specs/fault-proof/stage-one/bond-incentives.md) set the first bond at the Fault Proof Mainnet launch, 400,000 gas at 200 gwei, at "approximately double the cost to respond at the top level". Seven type 9 factories I queried, three on mainnet (OP Mainnet, Unichain, Ink) and four on Sepolia, set the root bond (`initBonds`) to 0.08 ETH, that same 400,000 gas. At 200 gwei, it is 157% of the example response's direct gas fee under Osaka (254,118 gas in replay) and 41% under Glamsterdam (976,078 gas). The bond equals the Glamsterdam response's direct gas fee at an effective 82 gwei. Mainnet dispute game creations over about a day I sampled paid 0.08–8.3 gwei. At 8.3 gwei, the example response's direct gas fee is about a tenth of the bond, so I'm not claiming a shortfall at those prices; the question is the sizing rule.

**One small fix.** `wasRespectedGameTypeWhenCreated` has a slot of its own: slot 9 in `SuperFaultDisputeGame`, slot 10 in `FaultDisputeGame` (and `PermissionedDisputeGame`, which inherits its layout). Slot 0 has room for it in both. With the flag packed there, a game created from the new implementation while its type is respected creates one slot fewer: 97,920 state gas, or 4.0% of the sampled type 9 creation and 4.7% of the type 1. Existing games keep their layout. `SuperPermissionedDisputeGame` already keeps the flag in slot 0. I haven't measured the execution-gas change of a patched build.

**Questions.**
1. Is the L1 cost of dispute game creations and moves under Glamsterdam tracked anywhere? I didn't find it in the bodies of #23015 and #23811, or in the titles of the nine public sub-issues of #20151. One of those, #19380, covers the PreimageOracle's reserved gas.
2. Should the root bond, and possibly the `getRequiredBond` curve, be revisited for Glamsterdam?
3. Would a PR for the packing be welcome?

I can share the traces, the per-transaction data and the scripts.

topPRs.title: op-reth!: launch the stock node from a launcher crate
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Builds on #24274 (step 3: op-reth as a library with overrides) and should be reviewed after it; the base branch is that PR's.

reth's launch stack (engine tree, pipeline, RPC registry, network, payload service, ExEx manager) is generic, so it is compiled in whichever crate launches a concrete node. `reth-optimism-node` launched op-reth's own node itself (`launch_node`, and `utils::setup` under `test-utils`), so it compiled the whole stack in the same rustc process as all of op-reth's components. That process ran the 16 GB CI executor out of memory (#20100, #20337, tracking #19935).

This PR moves the only instantiation of op-reth's stock launch into a new crate, `reth-optimism-node-launcher`, modelled on tempo's `node-launcher`: non-generic `launch` / `launch_node` functions that return boxed futures, so callers compile neither the stack nor its `poll` code. The `op-reth` binary, the integration tests that launch op-reth's own node and the `exex-hello-world` example go through it. `reth-optimism-node` no longer launches any concrete node. An embedder's `CustomOpNode` still launches through the generic `LaunchOpNode` in the embedder's crate, as in #24274.

No change for operators: the launch (proof history, Storage V1 warning, state-masking check) is the same code, now compiled in another crate.

### Compile memory

Peak RSS of each rustc process, from `/usr/bin/time -l` through a `RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER`, on an M-series Mac (16 cores, 64 GB). Both columns use CI's settings: `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` (`.circleci/continue/helpers.yml`) and `-j 8` (the 8 vCPUs of `xlarge.gen2`). Base is #24274's head `5d23396728`; after is this PR. These numbers are not comparable with #24274's table: incremental builds use 256 codegen units instead of 16 and peaked several GB lower here.

| command | debug base → after | release base → after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cargo build -p reth-optimism-node --all-features` | 18.7 → **0.74** GB (node lib) | 6.3 → **0.95** GB |
| `cargo test -p reth-optimism-node --all-features --no-run`, largest rustc | 18.6 (node lib) → **14.7** GB (`tests/it`) | 8.1 (`e2e_testsuite`) → 9.4 GB (`e2e_testsuite`) |
| same, summed RSS of concurrent rustc processes (sampled) | ~18.0 → **~14.0** GB | ~15.4 → ~13.9 GB |
| `cargo test -p reth-optimism-node --all-features --doc` | 1.4 → 1.0 GB | 4.8 → 3.0 GB |
| CI's `rust-build`: `cargo build --profile dev --workspace`, rebuilding what depends on `reth-optimism-node`, summed concurrent rustc RSS (sampled) | ~14.7 GB | **~14.4 GB** | |
| `cargo build -p op-reth` | 15.5 (node lib) → 15.7 GB (launcher) | 5.7 → 5.9 GB (`op-reth` bin, thin LTO) |

The other processes of the debug test build after this PR: the launcher 12.0 GB, `e2e_testsuite` 7.7 GB (base: 1.8), `tests/it` 14.7 GB (base: 8.3), the node lib 0.7 GB.

The example matters for `rust-build`, which builds the debug workspace on the 16 GB `xlarge.gen2`. `exex-hello-world` launched op-reth's node itself, at 15.3 GB of rustc. On base it had to wait for `reth-optimism-node`; without the example change it compiled at the same time as the launcher, the summed peak reached ~20 GB, and `rust-build` failed on this PR's first push. Through the launcher it compiles only its Ethereum half (9.3 GB) after the launcher.

What I infer from these:
- The launch stack was almost all of `reth-optimism-node`'s compile memory: the lib alone falls from 18.7 to 0.74 GB.
- The `op-reth` binary build is unchanged, as expected: it compiles the same stack once, in the launcher instead of the node lib.
- In debug, the test binaries got heavier. Debug builds share generic instances across crates, and on base `tests/it` and `e2e_testsuite` reused the copy that `utils::setup` (reth's E2E harness on op-reth's node) had compiled into the lib. Now `tests/it` compiles the three node types of the `custom_pool/` tests itself, and that is its 14.7 GB. Taking the E2E harness out of `tests/it` as well made no difference (14.9 GB), so this PR keeps those tests on the harness.
- Release builds share no generics, so there each test binary compiles its own copies before and after; the 9.4 vs 8.1 GB of `e2e_testsuite` is within the run-to-run noise I saw.

### CI executor

The affected job is `rust-ci-cargo-tests` (`rust-tests` in the `rust-ci` workflow), moved to `2xlarge.gen2` by #20100. It runs `just test`, which since #24192 also runs the doc tests that #20337 had moved to `2xlarge.gen2` in the former `rust-doctest` job. This PR does not make `xlarge.gen2` (16 GB) viable for it: the largest rustc process of its debug build is still `tests/it` at 14.7 GB, and the job compiles the rest of the workspace with up to 8 other rustc processes at the same time. Measured on macOS, not on the CircleCI Linux image. To get there, the `custom_pool/` tests' node types would have to be split across test binaries or launched through `OpNode::with_pool`; I left that for a follow-up. `op-reth-compact-codec` (`xlarge.gen2`, a debug `cargo run --bin op-reth --features dev`) is not helped either: a debug `op-reth` build peaks at 15.5–15.7 GB before and after (measured without `dev`).

### Review

`rust-code-reviewer` and `deletion-reviewer` ran on the diff. Dismissed or deferred:
- Make `launch` take `(builder, node)` like `launch_node`: kept taking a built `OpRethLaunchBuilder`, as tempo does, so a caller can still add hooks such as `extend_rpc_modules` before launching.
- Have the test helper set `num_state_masking_blocks = 0`: the tests launched with reth's default of 30 before this PR too; changing the tested config is out of scope.
- Re-export the launcher from the `reth-op` umbrella crate: not done; nothing uses `reth_op::node::launch_node`.

BREAKING CHANGE: `reth_optimism_node::launch_node` (also reachable as `reth_op::node::launch_node`) moves to `reth_optimism_node_launcher::launch_node`, which takes the same `(builder, node, hooks)` and returns a boxed future. `reth_optimism_node::utils::setup` (`test-utils`) is removed: build the nodes with `E2ETestSetupBuilder::<OpNode>::new(n, utils::chain_spec()).with_attributes_generator(utils::optimism_payload_attributes).build()`. Premium uses neither.

topPRs.title: op-reth!: expose node overrides through a shared library launcher
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Embedders currently have to reproduce op-reth's CLI and launch wiring to replace production components. This exposes a library entry point with extra CLI arguments, version metadata, and an async node mapper, so an embedding binary can replace the pool and payload service while inheriting op-reth's launch behavior.

Stock op-reth retains its defaults and concrete launch path. Customized nodes retain shared runtime configuration, derived-payload handling, proof history, debug launch, and shutdown. Async preparation lets an embedder finish required initialization before the pool starts accepting transactions; narrow hooks support RPC changes and tasks started with the node runtime.

BREAKING CHANGE: Rust embedders that directly access `OpNode` configuration fields or rely on its previous component types must migrate to `args()`, `builder_config()`, `standard_pool_builder()`, and the typed `with_pool` / `with_payload` setters. The node-level `with_da_config` and `with_gas_limit_config` setters are removed; mutate the shared handles returned by `builder_config()` instead. Binary embedders can use `main_with(OpRethOverrides::new().map_node(...))` instead of owning the launch sequence.

Validation completed locally: 62 op-reth/node library tests, the mapper doctest, targeted all-target Clippy, and documentation builds. Read-only subsystem and deletion reviews were also completed. This draft preserves the reviewed commits without a rebase. The node-level DA/gas-limit replacement setters and their mutable accessor have been removed; the shared-handle regression test captures builders before configuration updates. Committed runtime coverage of the mapper/hook boundary remains a review item. No node-wide EVM factory override is included.

topPRs.title: op-reth!: let a binary embed op-reth with overrides
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Step 3 of making op-reth-premium a thin "op-reth plus subblocks" wrapper. This PR is stacked on #24270.

Today premium copies op-reth's startup and launch code and defines its own node types, so changes to op-reth's launch never reach it. This PR lets a binary embed op-reth instead, the way tempo's `tempo_main_with(TempoOverrides)` works.

- **First commit:** `op_reth::main_with(OpRethOverrides)` runs op-reth with three additions:
  - extra `node` arguments, flattened after op-reth's own in `OpRethArgs`;
  - the embedder's version metadata;
  - one `customize` step. It gets the node config, the extra arguments and the `OpNode` op-reth built. It returns the node to launch, plus two hooks with concrete types: an RPC extension and an on-started hook.
- **Second commit:** `OpNode::with_pool` / `with_payload` return a `CustomOpNode`, with a replaced pool builder or payload service. `CustomOpNode` keeps its `OpNode` private, so changing a config field afterwards can't split the components from the add-ons.

These hooks are exactly the ones premium uses. I rewrote premium on this branch as a check, kept as a local, unpushed commit for the final premium PR:
- the rewrite deletes `PremiumOpNode`, `PremiumStandardSdmOpNode`, `SdmStandardPayloadServiceBuilder` and `launch_and_await_exit`;
- a small enum chooses between the subblocks and SDM-standard payload services;
- it is +282/−465 lines, excluding lockfiles;
- its clippy, unit tests (593) and in-process node tests (95) pass;
- the API needed no premium special cases.

**Effect on op-reth:** none at runtime. The `node` command line is unchanged; a test compares its help with the `Cli<RollupArgs>` one that the CLI snapshot pins. Startup order and logs are unchanged. One thing differs: a failure to install the version metadata now stops op-reth instead of printing a warning. That can only happen if another caller claimed the metadata first.

**Library users:** `launch_node` takes a third argument, `OpLaunchHooks`. Pass `OpLaunchHooks::default()` to keep today's behaviour.

**Room for kona (#23826):** op-reth's own `node` arguments go in `OpRethArgs`. A future that runs alongside the node can race `launch` in `main_with`, or go on `OpLaunchHooks`.

### Compile memory

op-reth's own launch stays non-generic, because a generic launch compiles in its caller's crate. Only a `CustomOpNode` launches through the generic `LaunchOpNode`, which compiles in the embedder's crate.

I measured the peak RSS of each rustc/rustdoc process with a `RUSTC_WRAPPER`/`RUSTDOC` wrapper that reads `getrusage`, on an M-series Mac. "Before" is #24270's head, `2bf0e403ab`. Wall times are noisy, because other builds were running on the machine.

`cargo build --release -p op-reth --bin op-reth` (the binary's own feature set):

| rustc process | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `op-reth` bin | 9.82 GiB | 7.98 GiB |
| `op-reth` lib | 0.12 GiB | 5.79 GiB |
| `reth-optimism-node` lib | 5.43 GiB | 5.54 GiB |

`reth-optimism-node --all-features`, the case that ran the 16 GB executor out of memory before (#20100, #20337, #19935):

| rustc process | debug before → after | release before → after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lib (`cargo build`) | 12.23 → 13.63 GiB | 6.85 → 6.93 GiB |
| lib unit tests (`cargo test --no-run`) | 9.01 → 10.56 GiB | 6.53 → 7.06 GiB |
| `tests/it` binary | 7.60 → 7.49 GiB | 10.76 → 11.86 GiB |
| doctests (`cargo test --doc`) | 1.36 → 1.36 GiB | 4.33 → 4.21 GiB |

What I infer:
- **The op-reth binary's peak falls.** The startup code moved from the bin to the new lib, so the two peaks no longer stack.
- **This PR raises `reth-optimism-node`'s `--all-features` peak by about 1.1–1.6 GiB.** That covers the debug lib, the debug unit tests and the release `tests/it` binary. These builds run on the 32 GB executor, but this works against #19935.
- **Likely cause (unverified):** the generic `CustomOpNode` path adds a layer of node types and impls that rustc compiles in the same process as the launch.
- **Follow-up:** the planned launcher-crate PR, stacked on this one, moves the launch out of `reth-optimism-node` and should take this back out. I did not work around it here.

### Behaviour changes for premium

There is no premium PR yet, so these are listed here.

- **Standard SDM path pool:** it now installs the policy pool instead of the stock pool, because one node type needs one pool type. Rules are rejected on that path, so the ruleset stays empty. This relies on `PremiumConfig::rules_enabled`'s documented claim that an empty-ruleset policy pool admits and orders like the stock pool.
- **Launch:** premium launches through op-reth's launch, which adds:
  - reth's debug launcher, which stays inert because premium still rejects `--dev`, `--debug.rpc-consensus-url` and `--debug.etherscan`;
  - the runtime state-masking guard;
  - the storage-v1 warning;
  - one more "Launching node" log line.
- **Startup:** op-reth's startup runs first:
  - the SIGSEGV handler;
  - `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` when unset;
  - the `--testing.sdm-fixed-policy` registry rejection and its TEST-ONLY warning;
  - the registry block-time default, which premium already applied.

  When both sides fail, op-reth's error comes first.
- **Build:** premium's `payload` crate compiles one launch instead of two.

These are unchanged, but now need a decision:
- `--proofs-history` is still ignored on the subblocks path and rejected without subblocks, although op-reth's launch could now serve it on both.
- The debug-launcher flags are still rejected.
- `--testing.sdm-fixed-policy` is accepted and logged as enabled, but neither premium payload service applies it.
- Premium declares no global allocator, so it runs on the system allocator.

### Reviews

- **Stale config:** `rust-code-reviewer` and `deletion-reviewer` both flagged that the first version of the second commit built the pool and payload service once, from public fields that could still change. The `CustomOpNode` wrapper replaces that design.
- I applied their other findings, except:
  - `+ OpNodeTypes` on the `LaunchOpNode` and `DebugNode` bounds stays. Without it the associated types don't normalize: removing it gives 88 errors.
  - the CLI snapshot test still uses `Cli<RollupArgs>`. `reth-optimism-cli` can't depend on `op-reth`, so the help-equality test lives in `op-reth`.

topPRs.title: op-reth: offload historical eth_getProof work with shared admission control
topPRs.author: bitwiseguy
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Historical `eth_getProof` requests currently perform synchronous work on async RPC workers, which can delay unrelated requests.

This PR moves that work to reth’s blocking worker pool and applies the existing `--rpc.proof-permits` admission limit. It holds each permit until worker completion and cleanup, including when the caller disconnects. It preserves existing proof computation and provider-error mapping; worker failures return an internal RPC error.

## Test

Regression tests cover async responsiveness, cancellation and cleanup, permit release after errors and panics, shared admission limits, and skipping queued work for disconnected callers.

## Related Issues
* Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/core-team/issues/3245
